name: Tripwire
title: Tripwire: Make Readiness Inspectable
payoff: Separate change compatibility from question readiness
idea: Tripwire makes an important distinction visible: a release can be compatible with an earlier analysis, while the evidence for a particular research question still needs attention. That distinction is worth building around.
terms: What changed for an existing analysis
Whether evidence supports the intended question
A recorded decision about a finding
framework: Start with the release, then the question, then the evidence. Tripwire separates these layers instead of asking one badge to carry every meaning. That gives the reviewer a more useful conversation with the data.
shots: overview-synthetic.png

This is the actual local Tripwire interface with invented data. It separates release compatibility from question adequacy. That helps the user see which claim each result supports, rather than reading every Ready label as the same promise.
request-evidence-synthetic.png

The review workflow also asks for reasons and roles. Our local checks confirmed that missing reasons and roles were rejected. The exported record preserved a request for more evidence, giving the next reviewer something concrete to follow.
strength: Another useful design is checking supposedly unaffected analyses. The source includes a rerun-and-compare path, and missing checks have an explicit insufficient-evidence state. Those are practical ways to make confidence earned rather than assumed.
next1: The next step is to make unresolved evidence requests stay visibly open. Recording a decision and resolving a concern are different events. Keep both states visible so the review counter tells the same story as the export.
next2: Then carry decision history forward. Retain the original evidence, the reviewer's reason, and each later revision. This builds on the existing reason-and-role checks without losing the context behind a changed decision.
prompt: Help me test Tripwire's review workflow with invented findings. Compare approval with a request for more evidence. Explain which concerns remain unresolved and what the exported history should preserve.

name: Identity Crisis Control Tower
title: Identity Crisis: Trace The Decision
payoff: Connect research questions, checks and review receipts
idea: Identity Crisis Control Tower connects a research question to its checks, measured effects, and human review. Its strongest idea is that a decision should come with a trail someone else can inspect.
terms: The intended use and its required checks
A digest tied to particular evidence
framework: A question card names what matters. Checks produce evidence. A review receipt records the decision. Keeping these connected makes it easier to ask why a result was reached and what would make it change.
shots: overview-synthetic.png

Here is the real local interface using invented data. It brings the research question and its evidence into one workflow. The useful design move is making the conditions behind the verdict available for inspection.
signed-synthetic.png

The review receipt records a person, a decision, and evidence fingerprints. The normal browser workflow produced a signed result. That is a useful foundation for accountable review, while the detailed audit explains the remaining binding limits.
strength: The analysis code also treats missing measurements explicitly instead of inventing a zero. That matters: zero is a result, while an unavailable measurement is a limit on what we can conclude. Preserve that distinction throughout the interface.
next1: The next step is one consistent rule for unavailable required checks. Keep the strict behavior across both the API and the browser. A development bypass should remain visibly incomplete and separate from an approved result.
next2: Then bind the entire review receipt to the evidence actually on screen. When the inputs or question change, withdraw the old approval and invite a new review. That turns the fingerprint idea into a stronger end-to-end contract.
recap: Keep evidence attached to the decision.
Refresh approval when its evidence changes.
prompt: Help me test Identity Crisis Control Tower with invented data. Change one required check and one input after review. Explain what should invalidate the old receipt, and show the evidence needed for a new sign-off.

name: Busy Beavers
title: Busy Beavers: From Finding To Review
payoff: Make data changes understandable and actionable
idea: Busy Beavers turns a data comparison into findings people can explore. It connects detected changes, affected analyses, and possible next steps. The useful idea is to make investigation feel like a coherent workflow.
terms: A detected change with supporting evidence
An input an analysis relies on
A new output that preserves the original
framework: Compare the releases, explain the effect, then invite review. Busy Beavers keeps those stages visible. A finding becomes useful when a person can trace it to evidence and understand which analysis it affects.
shots: results-synthetic.png

This is the actual local results screen with invented sample data. In our browser checks, a swapped profile exposed evidence and showed one analysis rerun while the unrelated analysis stayed unchanged. The interface makes that relationship inspectable.
next-steps-synthetic.png

The next-steps view carries the investigation forward. The tested swap path kept researcher review pending and did not automatically apply a fix. The downloaded findings also matched the information shown in the interface.
strength: The architecture preserves original releases and produces derivatives separately. That is worth keeping. It lets a researcher compare a proposed correction with the source rather than silently losing the earlier state.
next1: Next, make every approved derivative follow the review decisions exactly. A proposed exclusion, an accepted exclusion, and a rejected exclusion need different outcomes. Keep previews useful, but label their approval state clearly.
next2: Also check input validity before taking an unchanged-file shortcut. A valid unchanged release and two empty folders are different situations. Give each a clear result and a concrete next action.
recap: Show which analysis a change affects.
Make evidence and next steps inspectable.
Bind approved exports to review decisions.
prompt: Help me extend Busy Beavers using invented data. Compare a proposed repair, an accepted repair, and a rejected repair. Show what each export should contain and how to verify the original release stayed unchanged.

name: OncoSys Cohort Studio
title: Cohort Studio: See Who Remains
payoff: Follow cohort membership through each operation
idea: Cohort Studio focuses on a different part of the problem: building the research group itself. Filters and joins change who remains. This project makes those changes visible before we rely on the final table.
terms: The group selected for a research question
framework: Start with the sources, apply explicit steps, and inspect the resulting cohort. Count rows, samples, and people separately. A join can increase rows without adding people, and that difference matters to the analysis.
shots: result-synthetic.png

Here is the real Cohort Studio interface with an invented test fixture. The observed workflow connected cohort construction with its result and export. The useful feature is the ability to inspect how the selected group was produced.
result-synthetic.png

The underlying checks distinguish join inflation from repeated patients and retain selection rules. That is a strong analytical foundation: the tool asks what the rows mean, rather than treating a bigger table as automatically better data.
strength: The reproduction export records expected input hashes and includes the operation implementation. That moves beyond a prose recipe toward an executable account of the work. Keep the explanation and the runnable steps together.
next1: Next, make provenance status precise. An unavailable expected checksum should say unverified; a matching checksum should say verified. Those states give the researcher different evidence, even when both files can be read.
next2: Then separate a proposed automatic correction from an accepted change. Show the requested join beside the suggested join, retain the original run, and record the person's choice before describing an output as approved.
recap: Count rows, samples and people separately.
Keep proposed and accepted changes distinct.
prompt: Help me test Cohort Studio with invented tables. Build a join that multiplies rows, then propose a correction. Show rows, samples, and people before and after. Preserve the original steps and explain what a reviewer must approve.

name: SNS Cohort Control Tower
title: SNS Control Tower: Explain The Change
idea: SNS Cohort Control Tower makes the effect of a data change part of the conversation. It brings together before-and-after analysis, evidence, and repair simulations. That gives reviewers something more useful than a bare warning.
terms: A digest of specific file contents
A proposed outcome under stated assumptions
framework: Follow the chain from the earlier release to the change and then the new result. SNS records analysis dependencies and evidence. That structure helps a researcher investigate why an answer moved.
shots: results-synthetic.png

This is the actual SNS interface, run locally with invented data. The review exercised its engine, API, and browser. The results view makes the comparison inspectable, with evidence connected to the affected analysis.
export-synthetic.png

The export workflow is another useful part of the project. It gives the reviewer a concrete artifact to inspect. The next development opportunity is to keep the authority behind every proposed data change just as clear as the change itself.
strength: The output includes file-content fingerprints and distinguishes analysis failures from ordinary comparison. It also represents repair simulations. Keep those simulations clearly labeled as recovery relative to an assumed baseline, rather than proof of truth.
next1: Next, connect repair execution to explicit review decisions. A rejected exclusion must stay rejected, and a flag for investigation must not silently become a restoration. This preserves the human's intended boundary.
next2: Then make small or unfamiliar input layouts explicit. Recognize the schema or explain why it cannot be assessed. That extends the useful evidence-first workflow to the difficult cases where confidence should be lower.
prompt: Help me test SNS Control Tower with invented releases. Compare a repair simulation with an approved repair. Include a rejected exclusion and a small input table. Explain the evidence and review decision required before export.

name: HIPPA-cratic Cohort Studio
title: HIPPA-cratic: Build And Cross-Check
payoff: Inspect cohort steps and an independent SQL check
idea: This is the HIPPA-cratic team's Cohort Studio. It makes cohort construction explicit and offers a second way to check the result. The opportunity is to connect a readable workflow with independently inspectable computation.
terms: The group selected for a research question
Which entity each joined record represents
A second computation of the same steps
framework: Define the steps, build the cohort, then cross-check the computation. The project distinguishes sample-level and patient-level joins. That helps expose situations where records multiply or become linked to the wrong sample.
shots: overview.png

Here is the actual application using its explicitly made-up sample, lab, and visit tables. We selected biopsy samples with a lab record from the same sample. The dropdown steps make that request visible without needing an AI service.
steps.png

The cohort view shows what survives each step. This is a useful teaching and review feature: the researcher can see where membership changes rather than discovering a smaller final table without an explanation.
sql.png

The project also offers an independent DuckDB SQL check. It recomputes the same steps another way. Agreement is useful evidence about implementation, while the research question and the choice of steps still need human judgment.
strength: The export retains steps, counts, release identity, and fingerprints. Those are strong ingredients for a reproducible record. The next step is making reconstruction enforce the same input identity that the record describes.
next1: Bind caches and rebuild scripts to the recorded input contents. When a file changes at the same path, either refresh the computation or explain that the immutable release contract was broken. Keep counts and fingerprints on one snapshot.
next2: Also distinguish an empty cohort from an unresolved question about the filter. Zero eligible records can be legitimate. A misspelled value needs a different explanation and a different next action.
recap: Keep sample and patient joins distinct.
Bind reconstruction to the recorded inputs.
prompt: Help me test HIPPA-cratic Cohort Studio with invented tables. Build one sample-level join and one patient-level join. Compare the engine with the SQL check, then change an input and explain what must be refreshed or rejected.

name: Cohort Firewall
title: Cohort Firewall: Evidence And Policy
payoff: Connect measurements, explicit rules and review
idea: Cohort Firewall separates measurements from policy. It makes the rules behind a readiness decision explicit and attaches evidence to the result. That is a useful architecture for a system people must inspect and challenge.
terms: A signed record of selected result fields
framework: Measurements feed explicit rules, and the result goes to review. The project's evidence records include fields, limitations, remedies, and what would justify reconsideration. That gives the next person a concrete starting point.
strength: The review controls include a real restriction against approving a Blocked result, observed in the independent tests. Preserve that boundary while strengthening exactly which evidence and question the signature covers.
next1: Next, bind the complete question and evidence document to the approval. A signature can verify the fields it covers; it cannot protect fields left outside that contract. Make changes to either invalidate the old receipt.
next2: Then broaden the difficult-input tests. Newly eligible samples, duplicate identifiers, and malformed filters deserve explicit outcomes. That builds on the existing insufficient-evidence behavior instead of allowing an unexpected shape to end the workflow.
recap: Bind approvals to the complete evidence.
prompt: Help me test Cohort Firewall with invented data. Change the question after a result is signed, and add a newly eligible sample. Explain which checks must rerun and why the earlier approval must not silently cover the changed evidence.

name: ClearAnswer
title: ClearAnswer: Turn Claims Into Checks
payoff: Connect research claims to inspectable evidence
idea: ClearAnswer starts with what someone wrote: a research claim. Its architecture connects extracted claims to data tools, evidence, and reviewer decisions. That is a useful way to turn a fluent report into questions we can actually check.
terms: A statement that needs supporting evidence
A record of the computations performed
framework: Take a claim, identify the computation it needs, then inspect the evidence. ClearAnswer separates the agent, semantic, and data layers. That structure makes it possible to distinguish a plausible sentence from a checked numerical result.
shots: overview.png

This is the actual local ClearAnswer landing page. It invites the user to submit a research report. We are showing the interface only; no model-driven audit was run for this film, and no external model service was called.
strength: The source includes a bounded verification loop and explicit categories for questions the available data cannot answer. Those are valuable ideas. A useful auditor needs a meaningful way to stop and say that the evidence is insufficient.
next1: Next, check every part of a compound numerical claim. Match each quantity to its unit, denominator, and computed result. One correctly rounded number should not make a different unsupported statement look supported.
next2: Then preserve uncertainty all the way to export. Keep the original confidence, the computation trace, and the reviewer's decision distinct. The export should explain what was established and what still needs evidence.
recap: Use explicit data and semantic layers.
Check every quantity in a compound claim.
Preserve uncertainty through review and export.
prompt: Help me test ClearAnswer with an invented report containing two numerical claims. Make one correct and one unsupported. Show the computation evidence for each, and explain how uncertainty should survive a reviewer decision and an export.
